reason: This passage (Exodus 3:1-22) demonstrates the opposite of the statement. God explicitly identifies with Israel as 'my people' (עַמִּי), states that he has 'seen' (ראה) their affliction, has 'heard' (שׁמע) their cry, and knows their pain (יָדַעְתִּי אֶת־ מַכְאֹבָֽיו). God commits to delivering them from Egypt, bringing them to a good land, and being with Moses in this mission. The entire narrative shows God acting with loyalty and compassion toward Israel, responding to their suffering and covenantal obligations. There is no indication whatsoever that Yahweh considers himself without obligation to them or contemplates replacing them with another people.
